property.text: In post-merge Osaka fork, the ommers tuple in a Block must always be empty (zero length). This is the body-level enforcement of the ommers_hash == EMPTY_OMMER_HASH header invariant.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block with non-empty ommers list. Must be validated at body level, not just header level.

property.severity_justification: Consistency enforcement between header and body. Missing body-level validation could allow data smuggling via ommer fields.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block accepted with non-empty ommers.

property.text: Block transactions may contain any of the five supported transaction types (Legacy, AccessList, FeeMarket, Blob, SetCode) encoded as either Bytes or LegacyTransaction objects. The execution engine must correctly decode and process all five types without type confusion.

reachability.notes: Attacker includes transactions of various types in a block. Type confusion between Bytes and LegacyTransaction representations could cause incorrect processing.

property.severity_justification: Transaction type confusion could lead to incorrect execution, gas miscounting, or consensus splits.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate type confusion between transaction representations.

property.text: A Withdrawal object must be immutable after freeze() is called. All four fields (index, validator_index, address, amount) must be set before freeze and unmodifiable after.

reachability.notes: Withdrawal immutability protects against post-construction modification. The Engine API JWT prevents external access, but a buggy CL could exploit this.

property.severity_justification: Withdrawal mutability after freeze could allow modification of withdrawal amounts or addresses during processing.

property.text: All four Withdrawal fields (index, validator_index, address, amount) must be explicitly set during construction. A Withdrawal with any missing field must cause a construction error.

reachability.notes: Ensures withdrawal objects are always complete. Missing fields could cause incorrect ETH crediting.

property.severity_justification: Incomplete withdrawal objects could credit ETH to zero addresses or with zero amounts, causing state inconsistencies.

property.text: The execution layer must not independently verify withdrawal amounts or validator existence; these are trusted from the consensus layer. However, the withdrawal address must be a valid 20-byte Address and the amount must be a valid U256.

reachability.notes: A compromised or buggy CL could inject withdrawal objects with inflated amounts, causing unauthorized ETH minting. The EL trusts CL withdrawal data.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect withdrawal amounts from a buggy CL would cause unauthorized ETH minting, affecting the entire network's monetary policy.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires compromised CL. CL bugs should be reported to the CL team.

property.text: Withdrawal addresses must not be spoofed: the execution layer must credit ETH only to the address specified in each Withdrawal object provided by the consensus layer via the Engine API.

reachability.notes: Withdrawal addresses are determined by validator withdrawal credentials on the beacon chain. Only a compromised CL can provide incorrect addresses.

property.severity_justification: Spoofed withdrawal addresses cause ETH to be credited to wrong accounts. Detectable on-chain but irreversible.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires compromised CL. Report via Ethereum Foundation Bug Bounty.

property.text: The bloom filter bytearray must always be exactly 256 bytes. The add_to_bloom function must never read from or write to indices outside [0, 255].

reachability.notes: Bloom filter operates on log data generated from attacker-crafted transactions. An arithmetic error in index computation could cause out-of-bounds access.

property.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds write in bloom filter computation could cause memory corruption, crash, or incorrect bloom values leading to consensus splits.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate an input (log address/topic) that causes byte_index to exceed 255.

property.text: The bit_to_set value in add_to_bloom must always be in the range [0, 2047] after the 11-bit mask (AND 0x07FF) is applied. This ensures byte_index is always in [0, 255] and no out-of-bounds access occurs.

reachability.notes: If the 0x07FF mask is incorrectly implemented (e.g., 0x0FFF for 12 bits), bit_to_set could exceed 2047, causing byte_index to exceed 255.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect mask implementation causes different bloom filter outputs across clients, leading to receipt root divergence and consensus splits.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate incorrect mask value in a client implementation.

property.text: The byte_index computed in add_to_bloom must always be in the range [0, 255]. This is derived from bit_to_set being in [0, 2047] and the formula bit_index = 0x07FF - bit_to_set, byte_index = bit_index // 8.

reachability.notes: This is a derived invariant from PROP-0030. If the mask is correct, byte_index is guaranteed in range.

property.severity_justification: byte_index out of range causes memory corruption or panic, leading to node crash or consensus divergence.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate byte_index out of bounds.

property.text: The add_to_bloom loop must iterate exactly 3 times, reading 2-byte pairs at indices (0, 2, 4) from the keccak256 hash output. Each iteration must set exactly one bit in the bloom filter.

reachability.notes: If the loop iterates more or fewer times, the bloom filter will have incorrect bit density, causing receipt root divergence.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect iteration count produces different bloom filters, causing consensus splits between clients with correct vs. incorrect loop bounds.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a client computing bloom with wrong number of iterations.
